newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products - Gasolines diffs quietly weaken.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products - Gasolines diffs quietly weaken.

text.p: Gasoline differentials weakened in the U.S. Gulf, New York Harbor and Midcontinent, although players said market activity was fairly subdued Monday.
On the NYMEX, August gasoline eased 0.01 cent to settle at 60.04 cents a gallon and August heating oil gained 0.13 cent to end at 52.35 cents a gallon.
Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline changed hands late in the day at 2.65 cents under the August NYMEX price, the low end of the trading range seen Friday.
However, that level was stronger than the early day levels, when those barrels reportedly traded as low as 3.00 cents under the August, according to market watchers.
Traders put prompt A1 reformulated gasoline at about 3.50 cents over the M1 grade, or about 0.85 cent over the August NYMEX.

Distillate prices in the Gulf found some buying interest Monday, with prompt heating oil trading at 2.35 cents under the NYMEX, up about 0.15 cent, and prompt low sulphur diesel trading at 1.45 cents under the NYMEX.
"It's getting to that time of month, and we've got carry in the distillate market," said one trader, noting the modest increase in buying interest.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline differentials slipped to between about 3.25 and 3.50 cents under the August NYMEX, according to players, partially due to the lack of interest.
Reformulated A2 gasoline for prompt delivery traded at 1.65 cent over the August NYMEX, nearly even with levels established late Friday.
Nearby low sulphur diesel barrels also firmed Monday, traders said, to between 0.75 and 1.00 cent over the NYMEX, a gain of nearly 0.50 cent on the day.

Midcontinent differentials remain mostly steady and quiet in dull Monday activity. Group Three prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were weaker at 0.50 to 0.25 cent under NYMEX, continuing last week's loss of more than 1.25 cents. A deal even with the print was heard done.
Chicago prompt gasoline differentials were unchanged at 0.50/0.25 cent below the print, with 0.30 cent done in early midday trade.
"It's been very quiet all day," said a Chicago player.
